case_study_insert.main_stem: Keystone Fintech (KFX) is a public limited company in the financial technology sector, employing a workforce of 56. Founded in 2010 by Daniel Okafor, the business sells real-time payment processing and fraud-detection subscriptions to banks and merchants and operates a hierarchical structure with democratic leadership. KFX plans to invest $950,000 in a new real-time payments platform with AI fraud detection, financed by a $600,000 five-year bank loan and a $350,000 share issue. It has fixed costs of $325,000 a year, a variable cost of $5.40 a unit and a selling price of $11.90, and currently produces 96,000 units a year. KFX faces two problems: absenteeism in customer support has reached 8.5%, and communication breakdowns between shift teams have slowed incident response.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Market Research Summary — October 2026: A survey of 610 finance managers at client firms found 64% would adopt real-time payment processing within 12 months, and 55% cited AI fraud detection as the main reason. 42% first heard of KFX through LinkedIn. Support tickets fell from 2,100 to 1,640 last quarter; average first-response time is 5.2 hours and platform uptime was 99.6%. The transaction-defect rate is 1.9% of payments. 30 of 56 staff are engineers; on-the-job training on the payments codebase runs weekly, while off-the-job security certification at the tech college costs $1,300 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Keystone Fintech for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Technology Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank raised the base interest rate from 4.25% to 5.0%, increasing the cost of variable-rate borrowing for technology businesses. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 6.5% from $12.60 to $13.42 per hour from April 2026, raising wage bills across support and administration teams. (3) Cloud and data-centre costs rose 10.4% year-on-year, technology inflation is running at 6.6%, and business spending on fintech software grew 9.1% over the same period.

questions.question_text: KFX plans to fund part of its $950,000 payments platform with a $600,000 bank loan and a $350,000 share issue. Explain two advantages for KFX of using a share issue rather than the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Equity from a $350,000 share issue carries no interest charge and no obligation to repay, so it eases the cash burden on a business that already commits $325,000 of fixed costs a year and earns $6.50 contribution per unit ($11.90 − $5.40). With interest payable already rising from $24,000 to $40,000 in Appendix 2, avoiding extra debt service protects the 18.0% profit margin and leaves more cash to answer the 8.5% support absenteeism and the 1,640 support tickets still arriving each quarter.

Point 2: A share issue brings in new shareholders who may contribute specialist payments or compliance expertise and who share the risk of the $950,000 platform, so Daniel Okafor's existing backers are not solely exposed if uptake among the 610 surveyed finance managers falls short of the 64% who intend to adopt. Unlike the $600,000 loan, equity needs no collateral over company assets and cannot trigger repossession. The cost is dilution of ownership and a claim on future dividends, which may strain relations in a hierarchical structure.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to KFX's financing decision and platform launch.

questions.question_text: KFX is launching its new real-time payments platform. Consider national television advertising, targeted LinkedIn advertising, or exhibitions at banking and payments conferences. Which should KFX choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
National television advertising: A television campaign would build mass awareness of KFX's real-time payments brand across the country very quickly. However, most viewers are not finance managers or merchants who buy payment processing, so much of the spend is wasted, airtime is expensive for a 56-person plc financing a $950,000 platform, and the response cannot be measured directly.

Targeted LinkedIn advertising: LinkedIn allows KFX to target job titles such as finance manager and payments director, matching the 610 managers surveyed, 64% of whom intend to adopt real-time payments and 55% of whom cite AI fraud detection. The 42% who already discover KFX through LinkedIn prove the channel works, and spend can be scaled with measurable clicks and demo requests against the $350,000 share-issue budget while the platform beds in.

Banking and payments conferences: Exhibiting gives KFX live demonstrations of fraud detection to committed buyers and face-to-face relationship building with banks, which matters in a relationship-driven industry. The drawbacks are high stand, travel and staff costs, coverage limited to a few events a year, and difficult measurement of return.

Recommendation: KFX should choose targeted LinkedIn advertising. It reaches the exact decision-makers identified in the research, is measurable and affordable, and builds on the 42% who already find KFX there. Television is rejected as an untargeted and costly mass channel with no route to a B2B subscription sale, and conferences are rejected as too infrequent and expensive to carry the whole launch; KFX should add one flagship banking event later, once the LinkedIn pipeline is producing qualified leads.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited knowledge of the promotional options with minimal context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of KFX with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of KFX with a well-justified recommendation explaining why television and conferences are rejected.

questions.question_text: KFX has absenteeism of 8.5% in customer support and communication breakdowns between shift teams. Explain two benefits for KFX of introducing team working.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Team working gives the 56 employees shared responsibility for resolving incidents, so support staff cover for one another when 8.5% absenteeism occurs and the 1,640 support tickets a quarter still get answered. Shared goals also tackle the communication breakdowns between shifts by creating handover routines and a common view of open incidents, which should shorten the current 5.2-hour first-response time and protect the 99.6% uptime promised to banks and merchants.

Point 2: Working in teams gives members a voice and social contact, which raises motivation and can reduce the absenteeism that disrupts the 96,000-unit subscription base. In a hierarchical structure, self-managed support teams also take routine decisions faster, improving incident response without pushing every issue up the chain of command, and the pool of ideas helps engineers and support staff reduce the 1.9% transaction-defect rate while the $950,000 payments platform is launched. Because the 1,640 tickets must still be handled during the launch, teams also protect service capacity without adding staff.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to KFX's absenteeism, communication and service quality.

questions.question_text: KFX must upskill 30 engineers to build the real-time payments platform. Consider on-the-job training on the payments codebase or off-the-job security certification at $1,300 per employee. Which should KFX choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Weekly pairing on KFX's own payments codebase keeps all 30 engineers productive on real tickets and fraud-detection work, costs no fees and teaches the exact architecture, security checks and release process the $950,000 platform depends on. It suits a team already losing time to 8.5% absenteeism and shift communication breakdowns, and it protects the 1,640 support tickets a quarter that must still be handled. Its weaknesses are that senior engineers lose delivery time, bad habits can spread, and no external credential is earned, which matters when banks ask for evidence of certified security skills.

Off-the-job certification: The college security-certification course at $1,300 per employee gives structured, current knowledge and a recognised qualification for all 30 engineers, costing $39,000 — modest against a $950,000 investment funded partly by a $350,000 share issue. However, it removes 30 people from sprints during the launch, delays the platform, and the content is generic, so KFX still needs in-house follow-up on its own codebase after the course.

Decision: KFX should choose on-the-job training as the core method, with off-the-job certification for six security leads. It is cheaper, immediate and specific to the product, shields incident response and reduces the 1.9% defect rate where the work happens. Full off-the-job certification for all 30 is rejected because it withdraws the entire engineering function at launch, spends $39,000 on generic material and delays a platform being sold to 610 surveyed finance managers; certification can be extended once the system is stable. With 8.5% absenteeism and 1.9% defects already stretching the team, protecting live capacity matters more than a certificate.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to KFX.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of one or both training methods in the context of KFX.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both training methods in the context of KFX with a justified decision covering cost, disruption and security relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how KFX's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $11.90 − $5.40 = $6.50. Answer: contribution per unit is $6.50.

Formula: Margin of safety = Current output − Break-even output. Break-even = $325,000 ÷ $6.50 = 50,000 units, so substitution: 96,000 − 50,000 = 46,000 units. Answer: margin of safety is 46,000 units a year.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways KFX's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Break-even output of 50,000 units against 96,000 units sold leaves a margin of safety of 46,000 units, showing the platform can absorb a sharp dip in merchant sign-ups while still covering $325,000 of fixed costs.
2. Contribution of $6.50 lets managers test a transaction-fee discount sought by large banks: a 6% price cut to $11.19 would reduce contribution to $5.79 and raise break-even towards roughly 56,100 units, showing whether extra volume compensates for the lower margin.
3. The $600,000 five-year bank loan can be stress-tested against the 50,000-unit break-even point, ensuring subscription revenue stays high enough to service debt before further spending on the $950,000 platform.
4. Average total cost of $8.79 a unit ($325,000 ÷ 96,000 = $3.39, plus $5.40) benchmarks the new platform: cutting the 1.9% transaction-defect rate or lifting output lowers unit cost, while the 10.4% cloud-cost rise threatens to push it up.

questions.model_answer: (i) Contribution per unit = $6.50 | (ii) Margin of safety = 46,000 units | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: 46,000-unit safety margin versus 96,000-unit output; fee-discount modelling against the $11.90 price; stress-testing the $600,000 five-year loan; and unit-cost benchmarking at $8.79 against defects and the 10.4% cloud-cost rise.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate KFX's profitability by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for 2024 and 2025. Has KFX's profitability improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 40.4%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 43.9%
Profit Margin 2024 = 15.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 18.0%
ROCE 2024 = 10.0%
ROCE 2025 = 13.5%

Detailed workings: 2024 — revenue $1,980,000 − cost of sales $1,180,000 = gross profit $800,000; 800 ÷ 1,980 × 100 = 40.4%. Operating profit $297,000 ÷ revenue $1,980,000 × 100 = 15.0%. Operating profit ÷ capital employed $2,970,000 × 100 = 10.0%. 2025 — revenue $2,460,000 − cost of sales $1,380,000 = gross profit $1,080,000; 1,080 ÷ 2,460 × 100 = 43.9%. Operating profit $443,000 ÷ revenue $2,460,000 × 100 = 18.0%. Operating profit ÷ capital employed $3,280,000 × 100 = 13.5%.

Evaluation: Profitability improved on all three measures. The margin between sales and direct costs widened from 40.4% to 43.9% as subscription revenue grew and support tickets fell to 1,640; the bottom-line measure widened from 15.0% to 18.0% as revenue outpaced the rise in capital employed; and returns on capital rose from 10.0% to 13.5%, indicating the platform investment has so far been used efficiently. The main qualifications are that interest payable climbed from $24,000 to $40,000, so debt service now absorbs more of the operating profit, and that the 2025 result relies on retaining 30 engineers amid 8.5% absenteeism and converting the 610 finance managers surveyed — only 64% intend to adopt — into paying subscribers while cloud costs rise 10.4%. If sign-ups lag, the 18.0% margin could fall back towards 2024 levels.

Conclusion: KFX's profitability has improved. All three measures rose (40.4% to 43.9%, 15.0% to 18.0%, 10.0% to 13.5%) through wider margins and better use of capital rather than through extra borrowing. KFX should defend the gain by fixing the loan rate and holding the $6.50 contribution per unit as the $950,000 platform scales.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost of sales, operating profit, interest and capital employed movements and a justified conclusion on whether KFX's profitability improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for KFX of introducing biometric contactless authentication for its merchant clients.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Biometric contactless authentication strengthens the fraud detection that 55% of the 610 surveyed finance managers named as their main reason for adopting real-time payments, helping KFX win and keep bank and merchant subscriptions that underpin the 96,000 units sold each year. Faster, safer checkout also supports the 99.6% uptime promise and protects the $6.50 contribution per unit against the 10.4% rise in cloud costs, strengthening the case for the $950,000 platform financed by a $350,000 share issue.

Disadvantage: Biometric systems require new hardware and integration work, which would add to the $5.40 variable cost per unit or the $325,000 fixed costs and squeeze margins unless merchants accept higher fees. They also introduce privacy and data-security concerns for a 56-employee firm already facing a 1.9% transaction-defect rate and 8.5% support absenteeism; a failed or slow authentication could raise the 1,640 support tickets and damage the relationships with banks that a hierarchical structure depends on.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual development linked to KFX's survey data, costs, security and service.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base interest rate rise to 5.0%, the 6.5% minimum wage increase and the 10.4% rise in cloud and data-centre costs will affect KFX. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Base interest rate rise (4.25% to 5.0%): If KFX's $600,000 five-year loan is variable-rate, the 0.75 percentage-point rise costs 0.75% × $600,000 = $4,500 a year, modest beside $325,000 of fixed costs and largely avoidable by fixing the rate. Higher rates may also slow bank spending on fintech, but Appendix 3 shows fintech spending still growing 9.1%, so the direct threat is limited.

Minimum wage increase (6.5%, from $12.60 to $13.42): Each affected hour costs $13.42 − $12.60 = $0.82 more, equal to 6.5% × $12.60 = $0.82. No hours worked or individual pay rates are given in the insert, so an annual wage total cannot be honestly calculated; the defensible point is that support wages rise unavoidably, and with 8.5% absenteeism KFX may need extra cover, lifting the payroll further.

Cloud and data-centre costs (up 10.4%): Hosting sustains the 99.6% uptime and sits inside the $5.40 variable cost. The insert does not decompose that cost, so only a labelled upper bound is possible: if the entire $5.40 rose 10.4%, that would add 0.104 × $5.40 = $0.56 per unit, or 96,000 × $0.56 = $53,760 a year, pulling the $6.50 contribution down towards about $5.94. Even a fraction of that recurs on every subscription, and it cannot be removed by fixing a loan.

Conclusion: The 10.4% cloud and data-centre cost rise will have the greatest impact. It applies to all 96,000 units, hits the cost line that funds fraud detection and uptime, and is well above the 6.6% technology-inflation rate, so it cannot easily be passed on. The wage increase is second because it raises costs but cannot be quantified from the insert, and the interest rise is smallest and can be hedged by fixing the rate — both still require careful cost control while the $950,000 platform launches.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to KFX.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on KFX's costs, prices or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes with a justified judgement that cloud cost inflation has the greatest impact and why the others are smaller.
